# Pi-Bifrost

> Model-routing extension for the Pi coding agent. You configure tier pools and strategies. Bifrost selects a model from that policy, then Pi runs the real provider/model.

## Install

Requires Pi 1.0.1 or newer and at least one authenticated provider model in Pi.

```sh
pi install npm:pi-bifrost
```

Routing is on by default, and physical selection is the default. A saved configuration or runtime preference can change that state; `/bifrost debug` shows the active state. When no saved configuration, route file, runtime routing preference, or explicit routing override exists, Bifrost loads provisional model pools from Pi's catalog before generation and checks model access in the background. It saves successful generated pools to project `.pi/bifrost.json`. An empty `{}` file counts as no configuration; any configuration setting stops automatic setup. Init is optional. Probes can use provider credits or reach rate limits. If every probe fails, Bifrost leaves configuration unchanged and warns. Bifrost saves generated pools and routing settings; prompt text and credentials stay out of the file.

Run `/bifrost init` inside Pi to refresh the catalog and reconcile pools. It reuses probe results from the last hour when they cover the current catalog, and probes before proposing pools when they do not. Pass `-f` to force fresh probes. Init preserves other configuration fields and handwritten model entries. It asks once before saving; `--write` skips that question. A TUI and an RPC session can answer it; a session with no UI saves only when `--write` is present. The summary highlights membership changes; `/bifrost inspect` shows the full lists, rules, and default tier. Init probes can use provider credits or reach rate limits. The displayed save target is the file it writes.

Selecting `bifrost/auto` in Pi's model picker is a separate opt-in. Classification is enabled by default, and the active classifier can receive the current prompt on a local-cache miss. `/bifrost classifier off` disables that call for this Pi session. The choice lasts for the session; after restart, Bifrost uses `classifier.enabled`. If legacy state conflicts with `classifier.enabled`, classification pauses until you choose a session setting.

The separate classification cache can store normalized prompt terms. Set `cache.enabled` to `false` to stop cache use; saved entries remain until `/bifrost cache clear`. If no configuration exists, run `/bifrost init` to save starter pools, add `cache.enabled: false`, keep the pools, and run `/bifrost reload`. Generation still runs at the selected provider.

## Route

```text
prompt → tier → configured model pool → reliability filter → strategy → Pi model
```

Bifrost selects a tier from a tier prefix, rule, local classification cache, optional classifier, or configured default. An exact-model rule can bypass the tier. Strategies include `first`, `fastest`, `cheapest`, `cheapest_input`, `cheapest_output`, `largest_context`, `best_value`, and `random`. Init orders verified models by probe speed for `first` and `fastest` selection.

Persistent circuits skip repeatedly failing models on future turns, then allow controlled recovery. By default, usage and billing rejections pause models with the same configured Pi provider ID in Auto and physical routing. Pauses use configured provider IDs and recorded request errors; live usage limits and billing-account identity stay with your provider. A generic HTTP 429 pauses that provider briefly; the current prompt ends at that error and later turns use the pause.

Set `reliability.allowanceCooldownScope: "model"` to limit usage and billing pauses to one model. Set `reliability.enabled: false` to disable pause enforcement. In Auto, set `reliability.retryOnAllowanceExhausted` to `true` to enable one retry after an empty usage or billing rejection. Pi must prove the turn is empty and safe to continue. The retry defaults to `false`. See `docs/guide/reliability-and-cache.md`.

Physical selection is the default: Bifrost activates Pi's provider/model before generation. Selecting `bifrost/auto` in Pi's `/model` picker opts into per-request physical dispatch using the same routing policy. Pi's footer shows `bifrost/auto → provider/model`; assistant messages record the physical model that answered. Tool continuations and Pi-owned retries stay on the model that started the turn. The bounded Auto allowance recovery above is the one exception for an empty failed turn. Selecting a physical model pins it for the session.

## Controls

- `/bifrost preview <prompt>` resolves a route without generating or activating a model. An enabled classifier may receive the preview prompt. A leading tier name stays literal in the preview prompt. Use `/bifrost preview --json <prompt>` for one machine-readable result line prefixed with `[bifrost-json] ` on stderr.
- A message that starts with a configured single-word lowercase tier name uses that tier for one turn. You can type the prefix in either case. The prefix is removed before the model sees the message. Pinned sessions treat tier prefixes as ordinary text.
- `/bifrost pin` keeps the current physical model for the session. `/bifrost unpin` resumes routing.
- `/bifrost off` and `/bifrost on` disable or enable routing. Off or pin exits Auto using the last dispatched physical model, or a default-tier model before any dispatch.
- `/bifrost classifier test` makes a fresh classifier request; `/bifrost classifier status` shows safe operational state.
- `/bifrost reliability` shows active provider pauses and recovery trials. `/bifrost reliability reset --provider <id>` clears one known provider pause unless its recovery trial is active.

## Optional tier classifiers

Classifiers choose a tier; the tier strategy chooses the exact provider model. Backends: `prompt` (a Pi chat model), `typesafe` (direct TypeSafe/Jev transport), and `pi-native` (Pi's `classify()` API and catalog, shown only when supported). Explicit `classifier.backend` wins. Otherwise Bifrost detects Pi-managed TypeSafe credentials, then `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, and otherwise chooses prompt. The first routed request reports the detected backend and reason. An enabled classifier receives the current prompt and tier criteria. Bifrost does not send conversation history, source files, or the provider model pool to the classifier by default. Preview can also invoke the classifier. Confidence measures how concentrated the returned distribution is; treat it as a signal, not proof.

## Limits

Bifrost selects a model. Pi runs generation, and your provider account owns quota and billing. The local classification cache stores normalized prompt terms; treat them as sensitive. It keeps no assistant responses, tool output, or source files for replay. Switching models can fragment provider prompt-cache locality, so pin one model when context continuity matters. Bifrost does not guarantee better code, lower cost, lower latency, or cache savings; results depend on your pools, strategies, and provider behavior.
